newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbian government to draft privatisation law soon.
newsitem.headline: Serbian government to draft privatisation law soon.

text.p: The Serbian government hopes to complete a draft privatisation law to be put before the republican parliament at its fall session, Serbia's Minister for Private Enterprise Radoje Djukic said on Tuesday.
But he warned the transformation would not be overnight.
"Privatisation is a delicate issue. It is a very serious social process, and it is a process precisely because it lasts, and will last," Djukic told a news conference.

Djukic said it was a mistake to view the Serbian, or Yugoslav economy as being predominantly state owned and identified three basic categories of ownership -- social, mixed and the "authentic" private sectors.
"The authentic private sector generates half of Serbia's gross domestic product (GDP) and employs one million people, which is not insignificant," Djukic said.
Economists distinguish the "authentic" private sector from state enterprises privatised during a five-year programme of so-called ownership transformation.
In the first half of 1996, 175,000 private companies were registered in Serbia, of which 72,000 were active.
Mixed forms of ownership account for 25 percent of Serbia's economy, while the rest is state-owned.
Djukic said ownership transformation of Yugoslavia's strong public sector began in 1991 before the break-up of the former Yugoslavia and has been an ongoing, if slow, process.

"The Serbian economy has extremely large social capital installed in the social and public sector of the economy, and nobody has the right not to use such capital for development and overall progress," Djukic said.
He denied claims by the opposition and independent economists that the state was holding up privatisation because it was reluctant to give up control of the economy.
"Ownership responsibility is the key. It changes the system of behaviour and establishes new relations and values on the market, which lead to greater efficiency," he said.
"The process of privatization has begun, it cannot be stopped by anybody. It might be faster or slower, but it is an inevitability." -- Amra Kevic, Belgrade newsroom +381 11 2224305
